title: Supply under GST
outcomes: Determine whether a transaction is a supply under section 7.
Apply Schedules I, II and III.
Identify composite and mixed supplies and their tax treatment.

meta.exam_tip: For each fact, cite the exact Schedule entry; examiners award marks for the reason, not just yes/no.

concepts.title: Meaning and scope of supply (s. 7(1)) and Schedule I
body: Section 7(1): supply includes every form of supply of goods or services — sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal — made or agreed to be made for a consideration by a person in the course or furtherance of business; import of services for consideration, even if not for business; and the activities in Schedule I made without consideration.
Activities of a person (other than an individual) to its members or constituents for consideration are also supply; so a club supplying to its members is covered.

Schedule I (supply even without consideration): permanent transfer or disposal of business assets where ITC was availed; supply between related persons or distinct persons in the course of business (gifts up to ₹50,000 a year by an employer to an employee excluded); supply of goods by a principal to his agent or by the agent to the principal where the agent supplies on the principal's behalf; and import of services from a related person or own establishment outside India in the course of business.
"Business" is wide: trade, commerce, profession, vocation and adventure in the nature of trade, whether or not for profit, including connected activities and the activities of a club to its members.
concepts.analogy: Supply is the taxable event — first ask "is this a supply?", then "of what?", then "where?" and "when?".
concepts.work: Free samples to dealers on which ITC was claimed: no Schedule I entry covers them, so no tax, but the ITC must be reversed.

concepts.title: Schedule II: goods or services?
body: Schedule II settles whether an activity is goods or services: transfer of title in goods is goods; transfer of right in goods without title (e.g. hire) is services; transfer of title in goods where property passes later on full payment (hire purchase) is goods.

Lease, tenancy or licence to occupy land or building is services; job work on another person's goods is services; goods forming part of business assets put to private use or used by another person without consideration — services.

Construction of a complex or building for sale before completion certificate is services; works contracts and supply of food or drink as part of a service (restaurants) are services; renting of goods and agreeing to tolerate an act are services.
Supply of goods by an unincorporated association or body of persons to a member for consideration is goods.
concepts.analogy: Schedule II answers one question only — goods or services — not whether tax is payable.
concepts.work: Restaurant meals are services, even though food is goods, because Schedule II treats them as part of a service.

concepts.title: Schedule III and notified non-supplies
body: Schedule III lists activities that are neither goods nor services: services by an employee to the employer in employment; services of courts and tribunals; functions of MPs, MLAs and other elected or constitutional office-holders; funeral, burial and crematorium services; sale of land and, subject to the construction rule, sale of a completed building; actionable claims other than specified actionable claims (lottery, betting, gambling, horse racing and online money gaming).

Also covered: supply of goods from a place outside India to another place outside India without entering India; high-sea sales before goods are cleared for home consumption; and sale of warehoused goods before clearance for home consumption.
Section 7(2)(b): activities of the Central or State Government or local authorities as public authorities that are notified on the Council's recommendation are also non-supplies.
concepts.analogy: Schedule III lifts certain activities out of GST altogether.
concepts.work: Selling a plot of land is outside GST; selling a flat under construction before completion is a taxable service.

concepts.title: Composite and mixed supply (s. 8)
body: A composite supply is two or more supplies naturally bundled and supplied together in the ordinary course of business, one being the principal supply; it is taxed at the rate of the principal supply.

A mixed supply is two or more individual supplies made together for a single price where the items are not naturally bundled and can be supplied separately; it is taxed at the highest rate among them.
Indicators of natural bundling: consumers usually expect them together, a single price, elements usually advertised as a package and the main element being the reason for purchase.
concepts.analogy: Composite follows the main item; mixed follows the most heavily taxed item.
concepts.work: A hotel room with breakfast is composite (accommodation is principal); a gift box of chocolates and a toy at one price is mixed.

illustrations.title: One price, many items
illustrations.q: (a) Zenith Ltd. sells a laptop (18%) for ₹1,20,000 including a carry case, charger and one-year warranty, invoiced as one price. (b) A shop sells a festive hamper for ₹1,200 containing sweets (5%), dry fruits (5%) and a decorative lamp (18%) at a single price. Determine the nature of each supply and the tax.

head: Case
Nature
Rate applied
Tax ₹
rows: Composite: items are naturally bundled; the laptop is the principal supply
Mixed: items can be sold separately and are not naturally bundled; single price
solution.title: Section 8

solution.text: Ask: would a buyer expect these items together in the ordinary course of business? If yes, composite; if they are merely combined for a single price, mixed.

checks.label: Composite supply taxed at the rate of the principal supply (18%)
Mixed supply taxed at the highest rate in the pack (18%)

illustrations.title: Supply without consideration
illustrations.q: Examine whether these are supplies: (a) Hari Ltd., Mumbai sends goods to its own registered branch in Bengaluru free of cost; open market value ₹80,000 (18%). (b) A trader gives his son a television from stock on which ITC was taken, as a birthday gift. (c) A company gives its employee gifts worth ₹40,000 in the year. (d) Mr. Sen sells his personal car to a dealer.

Schedule I: permanent disposal of business assets on which ITC was availed

Not in the course or furtherance of business
solution.title: Section 7 read with Schedule I

jobs.title: Billing review
jobs.situation: A retailer bundles products into combo offers and asks what rate to charge.
steps: List each combo and its contents.
Ask whether items are naturally bundled.
Apply principal-supply rate or highest rate.
Consider pricing items separately to avoid the highest rate.
jobs.takeaway: Pricing items separately avoids mixed-supply treatment altogether.

mcqs.q: Which is a supply even without consideration under Schedule I?
options: Goods sent to a branch registered in another State
Free samples to customers on which ITC was not taken
Personal car sold by an individual
Gift of ₹20,000 by employer to employee
mcqs.explain: Branches with separate registrations are distinct persons, so stock transfers between them are supply even without consideration. Gifts up to ₹50,000 to an employee are excluded. In practice: value at open market value.
mcqs.topic: Meaning and scope of supply (s. 7(1)) and Schedule I

mcqs.q: Import of services without consideration is a supply when received:
options: From a related person abroad in the course of business
From any person for personal use
From an unrelated person for business
mcqs.explain: Schedule I covers import of services from a related person or from one's own establishment outside India in the course of business, even without consideration. In practice: tax is paid under reverse charge.
mcqs.topic: Meaning and scope of supply (s. 7(1)) and Schedule I

mcqs.q: Under Schedule II, hire purchase of goods is a supply of:
mcqs.explain: Where title in goods passes at a future date on payment of the full consideration, it is a supply of goods. Hire without title is services. In practice: check the agreement.

options: Services by an employee to the employer in employment
mcqs.explain: Employee services in the course of employment are neither goods nor services. The others are services under Schedule II. In practice: consultants are not employees.

mcqs.q: Which actionable claim is taxable under GST?
mcqs.explain: Only specified actionable claims — lottery, betting, gambling, horse racing and online money gaming — are taxable; other actionable claims are in Schedule III. In practice: value rules for these are special.

mcqs.q: Goods shipped from China directly to Brazil by an Indian trader, never entering India, are:
options: Neither supply of goods nor services
mcqs.explain: Supply of goods from a non-taxable territory to another non-taxable territory without entering India is in Schedule III. In practice: such turnover is still reported in returns where required.

mcqs.q: A mixed supply is taxed at:
options: The highest rate among its components
The rate of the principal supply
mcqs.explain: Section 8(b) applies the highest rate to a mixed supply. Composite supplies take the principal supply's rate. In practice: separate pricing avoids this.

options: Goods packed, insured and transported by the supplier to the buyer
A pack of shampoo and a free toy at one price
Diwali gift box of sweets and crockery
A combo of soap and a bucket
mcqs.explain: Packing, transport and insurance are naturally bundled with the supply of goods, the goods being the principal supply. The others are merely combined for a single price. In practice: tax at the goods' rate.

summary: Supply: for consideration, in course of business; plus import of services and Schedule I.
Schedule I: no consideration needed (assets with ITC, related/distinct persons, principal-agent, related import of services).
Schedule II: goods v. services; Schedule III: neither.
Composite → principal rate; mixed → highest rate.
remember: Employer gifts up to ₹50,000 a year are not supply.
Only five specified actionable claims are taxable.
traps: Separate registrations make branches distinct persons.
Sale of land is outside GST.

viva.q: What are the essentials of a supply under section 7(1)(a)?
viva.model: Supply of goods or services, for consideration, by a person, in the course or furtherance of business — any form such as sale, barter, exchange, lease or disposal.

viva.q: When are gifts to employees taxable?
viva.model: When the value of gifts given by an employer to an employee exceeds ₹50,000 in a financial year, as Schedule I treats them as supply between related persons.
Whether a particular activity is a supply of goods or a supply of services, such as treating job work and leasing as services and hire purchase as goods.
Services of an employee to the employer in employment and sale of land, among others such as funeral services and high-sea sales.

viva.q: How is a composite supply taxed?
viva.model: At the rate applicable to its principal supply, because the elements are naturally bundled with that main supply.

cases.title: Spark Electricals
cases.case: Spark Electricals, a registered dealer in Lucknow, (i) moves a generator from its Lucknow office to its separately registered Kanpur warehouse; (ii) gives its accountant Diwali gifts worth ₹60,000 in the year; (iii) sells a fan-and-light combo at one price; (iv) sells an old office building after completion certificate.

options: Not a supply, as both places are in one State
mcqs.explain: Each separate registration, even within the same State, is a distinct person, so the transfer is a Schedule I supply without consideration. In practice: value it at open market value.
mcqs.topic: Meaning and scope of supply (s. 7(1)) and Schedule I

options: Are a supply, as they exceed ₹50,000
mcqs.explain: Gifts to an employee above ₹50,000 in a year are a supply under Schedule I. In practice: value at open market value.
mcqs.topic: Meaning and scope of supply (s. 7(1)) and Schedule I

mcqs.q: The fan-and-light combo (iii) is taxed as:
options: A mixed supply at the higher rate
A composite supply at the fan's rate
mcqs.explain: The items are not naturally bundled but are sold at one price, so the highest rate applies. In practice: price them separately.

mcqs.q: Sale of the completed building (iv) is:
options: Neither supply of goods nor services
mcqs.explain: Sale of a building after the completion certificate is in Schedule III. In practice: ITC on related inputs may need reversal.
